views.name: taxi_yellow_trips_cleaned
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  vendor_id AS vendor_id,
  pickup_datetime AS pickup_ts,
  dropoff_datetime AS dropoff_ts,
  passenger_count AS passenger_count,
  SAFE_CAST(trip_distance AS FLOAT64) AS trip_distance_miles,
  CASE
    WHEN pickup_longitude BETWEEN -180 AND 180 AND pickup_latitude BETWEEN -90 AND 90 THEN pickup_longitude
    ELSE NULL
  END AS pickup_longitude,
  CASE
    WHEN pickup_longitude BETWEEN -180 AND 180 AND pickup_latitude BETWEEN -90 AND 90 THEN pickup_latitude
    ELSE NULL
  END AS pickup_latitude,
  CASE
    WHEN dropoff_longitude BETWEEN -180 AND 180 AND dropoff_latitude BETWEEN -90 AND 90 THEN dropoff_longitude
    ELSE NULL
  END AS dropoff_longitude,
  CASE
    WHEN dropoff_longitude BETWEEN -180 AND 180 AND dropoff_latitude BETWEEN -90 AND 90 THEN dropoff_latitude
    ELSE NULL
  END AS dropoff_latitude,
  rate_code AS rate_code,
  store_and_fwd_flag AS store_and_fwd_flag,
  payment_type AS payment_type,
  SAFE_CAST(fare_amount AS FLOAT64) AS fare_amount,
  SAFE_CAST(extra AS FLOAT64) AS extra,
  SAFE_CAST(mta_tax AS FLOAT64) AS mta_tax,
  SAFE_CAST(tip_amount AS FLOAT64) AS tip_amount,
  SAFE_CAST(tolls_amount AS FLOAT64) AS tolls_amount,
  SAFE_CAST(imp_surcharge AS FLOAT64) AS imp_surcharge,
  SAFE_CAST(total_amount AS FLOAT64) AS total_amount,
  -- derived duration in seconds (NULL when timestamps are missing or negative)
  CASE
    WHEN pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL AND dropoff_datetime IS NOT NULL THEN
      GREATEST(0, TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND))
    ELSE NULL
  END AS trip_duration_seconds
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_yellow_trips_2016`
grain: one row per taxi trip record
views.description: Cleaned projection of `tlc_yellow_trips_2016` normalizing types, removing clearly invalid geocoordinates, exposing parsed dates and common measures. Use this as a reliable taxi-trip input for aggregations, joins by date, and spatial filters. | Use for: time-series of taxi counts or revenue by day/hour; spatial pickup/dropoff heatmaps (after filtering NULL coords); fare / tip averages and distributions; trip-duration vs distance analyses

views.name: citibike_trips_with_station_ids
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  tripduration AS trip_duration_seconds,
  starttime AS start_ts,
  stoptime AS stop_ts,
  SAFE_CAST(start_station_id AS STRING) AS start_station_id_str,
  start_station_name AS start_station_name,
  SAFE_CAST(end_station_id AS STRING) AS end_station_id_str,
  end_station_name AS end_station_name,
  start_station_latitude AS start_station_latitude,
  start_station_longitude AS start_station_longitude,
  end_station_latitude AS end_station_latitude,
  end_station_longitude AS end_station_longitude,
  bikeid AS bike_id,
  usertype AS user_type,
  birth_year AS birth_year,
  gender AS gender,
  -- derived start/stop dates for easy date-based grouping
  DATE(starttime) AS start_date,
  DATE(stoptime) AS stop_date
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_trips`
grain: one row per citibike trip record
views.description: Normalized citibike trip records with station id fields cast to STRING to match citibike_stations.station_id and derived trip start/end dates and duration. Useful for joins to station metadata and time-based aggregations. | Use for: join citibike trips to station metadata by station_id; daily counts of trips per station or region; trip duration distributions by user type or age cohort

views.name: citibike_station_status_latest
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  station_id AS station_id,
  name AS station_name,
  short_name AS short_name,
  latitude AS station_latitude,
  longitude AS station_longitude,
  region_id AS region_id,
  rental_methods AS rental_methods,
  capacity AS capacity,
  num_bikes_available AS num_bikes_available,
  num_bikes_disabled AS num_bikes_disabled,
  num_docks_available AS num_docks_available,
  num_docks_disabled AS num_docks_disabled,
  is_installed AS is_installed,
  is_renting AS is_renting,
  is_returning AS is_returning,
  last_reported AS last_reported_ts,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY station_id ORDER BY last_reported DESC) AS station_rank
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_stations`
grain: one row per station reporting (station_id, last_reported) with rank; filter station_rank=1 for latest-per-station
views.description: Latest reported status per citibike station (one row per station_id) exposing capacity and availability measures and timestamp. Use for current-state dashboards and joins to trips for capacity-aware analyses. | Use for: current availability per station; capacity vs availability snapshots; joining latest station state to recent trips

views.name: nypd_collisions_core_metrics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key AS collision_id,
  timestamp AS collision_ts,
  DATE(timestamp) AS collision_date,
  borough AS borough,
  on_street_name AS on_street_name,
  off_street_name AS off_street_name,
  cross_street_name AS cross_street_name,
  SAFE_CAST(latitude AS FLOAT64) AS latitude,
  SAFE_CAST(longitude AS FLOAT64) AS longitude,
  COALESCE(number_of_persons_injured, 0) AS persons_injured,
  COALESCE(number_of_persons_killed, 0) AS persons_killed,
  COALESCE(number_of_pedestrians_injured, 0) AS pedestrians_injured,
  COALESCE(number_of_pedestrians_killed, 0) AS pedestrians_killed,
  COALESCE(number_of_cyclist_injured, 0) AS cyclists_injured,
  COALESCE(number_of_cyclist_killed, 0) AS cyclists_killed,
  COALESCE(number_of_motorist_injured, 0) AS motorists_injured,
  COALESCE(number_of_motorist_killed, 0) AS motorists_killed,
  vehicle_type_code1 AS vehicle_type_code1,
  contributing_factor_vehicle_1 AS contributing_factor_vehicle_1
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.nypd_mv_collisions`
views.description: Normalized projection of NYPD motor vehicle collisions exposing temporal, location, and injury/fatality measures. Use for safety trend analysis and spatial joins. | Use for: daily collision counts and severity; spatial distribution of collisions; injury/fatality trends by borough or vehicle type

views.name: service_requests_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key AS request_id,
  created_date AS created_ts,
  closed_date AS closed_ts,
  DATE(created_date) AS created_date,
  agency AS agency,
  agency_name AS agency_name,
  complaint_type AS complaint_type,
  descriptor AS descriptor,
  status AS status,
  borough AS borough,
  community_board AS community_board,
  incident_zip AS incident_zip,
  incident_address AS incident_address,
  SAFE_CAST(latitude AS FLOAT64) AS latitude,
  SAFE_CAST(longitude AS FLOAT64) AS longitude
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.311_service_requests`
views.description: Cleaned 311 service requests projection with parsed dates, borough and coordinates. Use for time-series of complaints, spatial joins, and status analysis. | Use for: counts of complaints by type over time; time-to-close analysis by agency or borough; spatial clustering of complaint types

views.name: tree_census_species_joinable
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  recordid AS record_id,
  address AS address,
  house_number AS house_number,
  street AS street,
  borough AS borough,
  longitude AS longitude,
  latitude AS latitude,
  species AS species_code,
  spc_common AS species_common,
  spc_latin AS species_latin,
  diameter AS diameter_cm,
  status AS status,
  location AS location_description
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_1995`
views.description: Denormalized tree census rows with both common and latin species names plus geolocation and status for easy joining to species metadata or spatial analyses. | Use for: species distribution across boroughs; join to tree_species by species common or latin name; diameter (size) distribution analyses

views.name: taxi_pickup_hourly_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(pickup_datetime, HOUR) AS pickup_hour,
  COUNT(1) AS trips_count,
  SUM(fare_amount) AS total_fare_amount,
  AVG(trip_distance) AS avg_trip_distance_miles,
  AVG(tip_amount) AS avg_tip_amount
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_yellow_trips_2016`
GROUP BY pickup_hour
ORDER BY pickup_hour
grain: one row per pickup_hour time bucket
views.description: Hourly aggregated measures for yellow taxi pickups: counts, total fares, average trip distance and average tip. Exposes pickup_hour to enable time-of-day trend analyses and downstream top-k by hour via ranking. | Use for: hourly taxi demand and revenue patterns; compare tip rates by hour; feed for time-series visualizations

views.name: collisions_daily_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  DATE(timestamp) AS collision_date,
  borough AS borough,
  COUNT(1) AS collisions_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(number_of_persons_injured, 0)) AS total_persons_injured,
  SUM(COALESCE(number_of_persons_killed, 0)) AS total_persons_killed
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.nypd_mv_collisions`
GROUP BY collision_date, borough
ORDER BY collision_date, borough
views.description: Daily aggregated collision counts and sums of injuries/fatalities, partitioned by borough. Useful for trend detection and joins to daily weather or events. | Use for: daily safety trends by borough; join to weather or events by date and borough
